app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` with no `require 'open-uri'` in this file. ruby-readability 0.5.7 does not require it, and the only `require 'open-uri'` is in poll_feed.rb, not loaded on the import_remote paths from topic_retriever.rb:51 or disqus.thor:146. NoMethodError/wrong-open on those paths.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content` is nil for plain RSS 2.0 (simple-rss 1.3.1 stores <description> as `description`, <content:encoded> as `content_encoded`; only Atom populates `content`). `nil.scrub` raises; with `retry: false` the hourly job silently dies for every RSS feed. `String#scrub` also needs Ruby >= 2.1, unpinned anywhere in Gemfile/lockfile.

app/models/post.rb:133 + poll_feed.rb:35 + best.html.erb:19 — Stored XSS (OWASP A03): raw_html cook_method makes `cooked == raw`, bypassing the entire sanitization pipeline; third-party feed HTML flows in via `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` (which actively re-enables escaped markup) and is rendered with `raw post.cooked` in both the embed iframe and normal topic views. poll_feed does not even apply the Readability tag whitelist that import_remote uses.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Unauthenticated stored XSS: `"#{url}"` interpolates the URL into HTML unescaped, stored with cook_method raw_html. EmbedController accepts arbitrary `embed_url` from anonymous requests and only the *host* is checked (topic_retriever.rb:15); path/query are unvalidated. `?embed_url=http://allowed-host.com/x'>` lands verbatim in a post.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — SSRF (A10): `open(url).read` after only a pre-fetch host check. open-uri follows redirects transparently, so a 302 to 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1:6379 is fetched, and the body is then stored as a post — exfiltrating internal responses. No scheme allowlist, no private-IP check, no redirect limit.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`: `Kernel#open` treats a leading `|` as a shell pipe (RCE as the Sidekiq user) and a bare path as a local file read. Admin-only input, but escalates a settings write to host compromise. Use URI.parse + Net::HTTP.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Broken access control (A01): `Referer` host equality is the *sole* gate on a public endpoint. Trivially spoofed with curl; any anonymous client reaches `best`, enqueues retrieve_topic and drives the SSRF above. The Redis throttle (topic_retriever.rb:26) keys on the full URL, so varying the path defeats it — unbounded outbound fetches, unbounded auto-created topics, unbounded Redis key growth.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — `X-Frame-Options: "ALLOWALL"` is not a valid XFO token, so browsers ignore the header entirely and the page is framable by ANY origin, not just embeddable_host. No `CSP: frame-ancestors` compensates. The framed page renders authenticated content via `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, ...)` — cross-origin clickjacking target.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin match. Passes for any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. `https://discourse.example.co` vs `...example.com`), and `indexOf("")` is 0 so empty-origin (sandboxed/data:) frames pass. Should be strict equality.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — `postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` derives targetOrigin from a spoofable request header and reflects the full referer URL into an inline <script>. ERB escaping prevents breakout here, so not directly exploitable, but the origin must come from SiteSetting.embeddable_host.

In `Jobs::PollFeed`, `content` is built from `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passed into `TopicEmbed.import` without any tag/attribute whitelist or sanitization (unlike `import_remote`, which uses Readability with explicit `tags`/`attributes`). The embed view renders this with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for these posts `post.cooked == post.raw`, so arbitrary feed HTML can be stored and rendered as-is, enabling stored XSS via `<script>`/event handlers/etc. This is directly verifiable from the added code paths in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Unauthenticated stored XSS: `"#{url}"` interpolates the URL into HTML unescaped, stored with cook_method raw_html. EmbedController accepts arbitrary `embed_url` from anonymous requests and only the *host* is checked (topic_retriever.rb:15); path/query are unvalidated. `?embed_url=http://allowed-host.com/x'>` lands verbatim in a post.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — SSRF (A10): `open(url).read` after only a pre-fetch host check. open-uri follows redirects transparently, so a 302 to 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1:6379 is fetched, and the body is then stored as a post — exfiltrating internal responses. No scheme allowlist, no private-IP check, no redirect limit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` on a URL ultimately derived from the `embed_url` request param (`EmbedController#best` -> `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). Although `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` before calling `import_remote`, that check only applies to the *initial* URL. Ruby’s `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects transparently, so an allowed-host URL can 30x-redirect to an internal/private address (e.g., 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254) and `open(url).read` will fetch it. There is no scheme allowlist enforcement beyond the initial host check, no private-IP/rfc1918 filtering, and no redirect handling/limit in this code, making SSRF via redirects a verifiable issue in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`: `Kernel#open` treats a leading `|` as a shell pipe (RCE as the Sidekiq user) and a bare path as a local file read. Admin-only input, but escalates a settings write to host compromise. Use URI.parse + Net::HTTP.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`. In Ruby, `Kernel#open` (even when extended by open-uri) will treat strings beginning with `|` as a shell pipeline and will also open local file paths, so a setting value like `|id` or `/etc/passwd` would be interpreted as command execution / local file read. Since `feed_polling_url` is admin-controlled (SiteSetting), this is an actual security risk introduced by the diff (escalates settings write to code execution under the Sidekiq process user).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Broken access control (A01): `Referer` host equality is the *sole* gate on a public endpoint. Trivially spoofed with curl; any anonymous client reaches `best`, enqueues retrieve_topic and drives the SSRF above. The Redis throttle (topic_retriever.rb:26) keys on the full URL, so varying the path defeats it — unbounded outbound fetches, unbounded auto-created topics, unbounded Redis key growth.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — `X-Frame-Options: "ALLOWALL"` is not a valid XFO token, so browsers ignore the header entirely and the page is framable by ANY origin, not just embeddable_host. No `CSP: frame-ancestors` compensates. The framed page renders authenticated content via `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, ...)` — cross-origin clickjacking target.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin match. Passes for any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. `https://discourse.example.co` vs `...example.com`), and `indexOf("")` is 0 so empty-origin (sandboxed/data:) frames pass. Should be strict equality.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both point out that using `indexOf` for origin validation is unsafe because it performs a substring check and can be bypassed by attacker-controlled origins that appear within the trusted URL (e.g., lookalike/malicious domains). The candidate even expands on additional bypass cases, but it’s the same core flaw.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — `postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` derives targetOrigin from a spoofable request header and reflects the full referer URL into an inline <script>. ERB escaping prevents breakout here, so not directly exploitable, but the origin must come from SiteSetting.embeddable_host.
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that `postMessage` is using the full `request.referer` URL as `targetOrigin` and states the origin should be derived from a configured host (i.e., scheme+host+port), aligning with the golden issue that using the full URL breaks postMessage delivery (and thus resizing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` combined with TopicEmbed.import passing `skip_validations: true` means remote content updates existing posts with all model validations (length, spam/link checks) disabled. The update path for the XSS findings has no server-side guard.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor to honor `skip_validations` by saving with `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path explicitly calls `revisor.revise!(user, ..., skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)`, so updates of remotely-fetched/embed content will persist without running ActiveRecord validations. This is directly verifiable in the diff and means any validation-based safeguards (e.g., length/format constraints or other validation hooks) are bypassed for these remote updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_creator.rb:216 — PostCreator now accepts a cook-pipeline bypass (`cook_method: raw_html` ⇒ unsanitized raw) from any caller, with no guardian or whitelist check at this boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `Post.cook_methods` enum and changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which typically includes sanitization and other safety/formatting steps). In `lib/post_creator.rb`, a new line sets `post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method]` whenever it is present, without any guard/whitelist check at this layer. This means any caller that can influence `PostCreator` options can request `cook_method: raw_html` and cause unsanitized HTML to be stored/served as cooked content. The new feed import path also uses this (`TopicEmbed.import` passes `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`) while `PollFeed` takes `i.content` from RSS and does not sanitize it before posting, making the bypass practically reachable and security-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `force: true` on a new create_table silently DROPs a pre-existing topic_embeds table instead of failing loudly.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop an existing `topic_embeds` table before creating it. That can silently destroy existing data if the table already exists (e.g., from a previous run/branch/misapplied migration) instead of raising an error, so the finding is accurately describing a real risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4-5 — topic_id/post_id have no FK, no index, and no `dependent: :destroy`. Deleting a topic/post leaves dangling rows; topic_id_for_embed then returns a dead id and embed#best raises forever for that URL with no repair path.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4-5 — no UNIQUE on topic_id/post_id though the model treats the relation as 1:1 (`embed.post` singular); two embed URLs pointing at one topic is representable and would make the update path fight over one post.

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with a UNIQUE index on `embed_url`, and the import/update logic always looks up by `embed_url` (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and creates a new topic/post when that URL is new. Nothing in the diff creates multiple `TopicEmbed` rows for the same `post_id`/`topic_id`, so the alleged “two embed URLs pointing at one topic/post making the update path fight” would only occur if data were manually corrupted/inserted outside this code. Also, `belongs_to :post`/`:topic` does not imply a 1:1 constraint; it allows many embeds to reference the same post/topic by design. Therefore the finding is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255) and carries the UNIQUE btree index; real embed URLs routinely exceed that and hard-fail at insert. Needs :text + hash/expression index, or an explicit limit plus a model length validation.

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as a `string` with no explicit limit, which in Rails defaults to 255 bytes/chars on common DBs (e.g., varchar(255)). The code stores arbitrary remote URLs from RSS (`i.link` / `i.id`) and from `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / `TopicRetriever` into `embed_url` and enforces uniqueness via `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`. If a fetched/embed URL exceeds 255, inserts/updates can fail at the DB level (e.g., PG rejects over-length varchar), breaking feed import / embedding. There is no model length validation or explicit larger column type to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `default: 1` hardcodes the Enum ordinal rather than referencing `Post.cook_methods[:regular]` (the value is currently correct — Enum is 1-based — but the DB default is decoupled from the enum). No CHECK constraint, so out-of-range discriminators are representable and Post#cook silently falls through.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `cook_method` as an integer with `default: 1` and the enum is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, so the DB default is indeed a literal rather than derived from the enum. However, this is not a concrete defect introduced by the diff: migrations typically should not reference application model code/constants (which can change over time), so hardcoding the default is common/acceptable. The lack of a DB CHECK constraint / model validation for enum range is also a general design choice and not a verifiable bug here, and `Post#cook` falling back to the normal cooking pipeline for unknown values is not clearly incorrect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-30 — check-then-insert TOCTOU: `where(embed_url:).first` then `create!`. The unique index prevents corruption but concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic runs raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique out of a job that has already created a topic+post. Needs rescue-and-reload or upsert.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to create a post/topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!` (inside a transaction). Because there is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, two concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g., PollFeed + RetrieveTopic, or two RetrieveTopic jobs) can both observe `embed.blank?` and race to `create!`, causing the loser to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue/reload/upsert logic, so the job/request can error even though the uniqueness constraint prevents duplicate rows. The transaction likely rolls back the second topic/post, but the unhandled exception is still a real correctness/robustness problem under concurrency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:34-38 — `revise!` return value ignored and `update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` runs unconditionally, outside a transaction. A failed/refused revision still advances the sha, so the next poll sees a match and the content NEVER re-syncs. Permanent silent divergence.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — Post includes Trashable (verified, post.rb:16), so `embed.post` is nil for a soft-deleted post and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises. Soft-delete is unhandled in this state machine.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally instantiates `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the content hash changes. There is no guard for `post` being `nil`. Even though `topic_embeds.post_id` is `null: false`, the associated `Post` can be unavailable to the association (e.g., soft-deleted with a default scope from `Trashable`, or otherwise missing), in which case `embed.post` will return `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise. The diff introduces this unhandled case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:23-29 — if `creator.create` returns nil or a post with errors, the topic is created but no TopicEmbed row is. topic_id_for_embed keeps missing, so every subsequent request creates ANOTHER duplicate topic. No error raised or logged.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — a *scheduled* job class is instantiated and run inline from inside a regular job. Every cache-miss embed request re-imports the entire feed; N concurrent misses run N full feed imports racing on the same unique index. No re-entrancy guard.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true and the embed URL hasn’t been seen yet. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` always fetches and parses the full feed and loops through all items, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for each, with no throttling/lock around the feed poll itself (the only Redis throttle is per-`@embed_url` in `retrieved_recently?`, not per-feed). If multiple TopicRetriever instances run concurrently (e.g., different cache-miss embed URLs, or multiple processes before the scheduled job runs), they will each re-import the entire feed and can race on `topic_embeds.embed_url`’s unique index because `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic “check then create!” (`where(...).first` then `create!`), which can raise on unique constraint under concurrency. There is no re-entrancy guard or lock to prevent N concurrent feed polls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-30 — the throttle key is claimed before any work succeeds, so a failed retrieval blocks retries for 60s. Staff bypass it entirely (no_throttle), and loading.html.erb auto-reloads every 30s — a staff member on that page triggers an unthrottled remote fetch every 30 seconds.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the Redis throttle key (setnx + expire 60) is written before any retrieval work happens; retrieve() then calls perform_retrieve, which can fail (e.g., network/open(url) in TopicEmbed.import_remote) without clearing the key. That means a failed fetch still blocks non-staff retries for 60s, matching the finding. Separately, Jobs::RetrieveTopic passes no_throttle: user.try(:staff?), so staff bypass retrieved_recently? entirely. EmbedController#best enqueues :retrieve_topic when no TopicEmbed exists and renders loading.html.erb, which reloads every 30s; if a staff user is the current_user and the embed never gets created (e.g., fetch fails), each reload enqueues another unthrottled retrieval job, leading to repeated remote fetch attempts about every 30 seconds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 — `feed_key` ("feed-modified:") is defined but never read or written. The intended conditional-GET / not-modified short-circuit was never wired up; every hourly run refetches and re-imports the whole feed.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` (which builds a Redis-like key `"feed-modified:..."`) is defined but never referenced anywhere in this diff. The actual `poll_feed` implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates all items, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for each, with no use of `feed_key` to short-circuit fetching/processing based on a stored “last modified”/etag or similar. So the “defined but never used / not wired up” part is directly verifiable, and it implies the job will refetch/process the feed on every run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — no rescue and no timeout around open()/SimpleRSS.parse; with `retry: false` any 404/TLS/redirect/malformed-feed error silently does nothing until the next hour, unlogged.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs a network fetch and parse with no explicit timeout handling and no `rescue` around either operation. Both `open(...)` (open-uri) and `SimpleRSS.parse` can raise on DNS/TLS/HTTP errors, redirects, or malformed feeds; with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, such failures won’t be retried by Sidekiq until the next scheduled run. The “unlogged/silent” part is overstated (Sidekiq typically logs job exceptions), but the lack of timeout/rescue around this external I/O is a real reliability defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31-37 — unbounded loop over feed items with no per-item rescue, no limit, no batching; one bad entry abandons every later entry.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `rss.items.each do |i| ... end` processes all feed items with no explicit limit/batching and no `rescue` inside the loop. Any exception raised while handling an item (e.g., `i.content` being nil causing `i.content.scrub` to raise, or unexpected item structure) will abort `poll_feed` and prevent processing of subsequent items. This reliability/correctness risk is directly observable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — `i.id` is Atom-only; RSS exposes `guid`. If neither yields an http(s) URL, TopicEmbed.import returns nil silently with no log.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each item’s URL is derived as `url = i.link` with a fallback to `i.id` when `link` is blank or non-HTTP(S). For many RSS feeds the unique identifier is exposed as `guid` rather than `id`, so this fallback can yield `nil` (or a non-URL identifier), and then `TopicEmbed.import` immediately returns `nil` due to `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` with no logging or error handling. This means some feed items can be skipped silently, which is a correctness defect in the new feed importer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 + :44-53 — `open(url).read` has no timeout, no size cap, and no rescue; the entire remote response is materialized in a worker, and RetrieveTopic dies on any dead/slow URL. `doc.title` can be nil → PostCreator with a nil title.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` with `open-uri` but does not set `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, does not limit response size, and does not rescue network/parsing exceptions (`OpenURI::HTTPError`, `Timeout::Error`, etc.). This method is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which is called by the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` worker, and that worker also has no exception handling—so a dead/slow/bad URL can raise and fail the job. Also, `opts[:title] || doc.title` can be `nil` if Readability doesn't extract a title, and that `title` is passed into `PostCreator` (with `skip_validations: true`), meaning it can attempt to create a topic/post with a nil title.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56-57 — `absolutize_urls` calls URI(url) unguarded; import's only validation is the `^https?://` regex, so a URL with a space or raw unicode passes it and then raises URI::InvalidURIError inside the transaction.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which only checks the scheme prefix and will accept strings like `"http://example.com/has a space"` (or other characters URI rejects). When creating a new embed, it then calls `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, which does `uri = URI(url)` without any rescue. `URI()` can raise `URI::InvalidURIError` for such inputs, and that exception is unhandled (it occurs inside the transaction block), so the import job/request can crash rather than gracefully skipping the item. This is a real, verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — TopicView.new raises for a deleted topic or one moved to a restricted category; a stale TopicEmbed row makes that embed permanently 500 with no rescue or fallback to the loading path.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the code treats the presence of a TopicEmbed row as authoritative: it does `topic_id = TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and if that returns a value it unconditionally does `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`. There is no check that the topic still exists, that the embedded user can still access it (e.g., category permissions changed), or that the TopicEmbed row still points to a valid topic/post. If `TopicView.new` raises (likely when the topic is missing or not visible), the controller does not rescue and also does not fall back to the `else` branch that enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`. Additionally, because a stale TopicEmbed row causes `topic_id_for_embed` to keep returning a non-nil id, the recovery path (enqueue/retrieve) will never be triggered for that URL. This makes the embed endpoint fail persistently for that URL until the row is cleaned up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — `params.require` raises ParameterMissing → 500, not the 404 the spec's title claims ("is 404 without an embed_url" only asserts `should_not be_success`).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `params.require(:embed_url)` will indeed raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when the param is absent, so the action won’t explicitly render a 404. However, the finding’s “→ 500” conclusion is not verifiable from the diff: in Rails this exception is typically mapped to a 400 Bad Request (or may be raised in controller specs depending on exception handling), not inherently a 500. Also, the spec does not actually assert a 404; it only asserts `should_not be_success`, so there is no concrete, diff-verifiable defect demonstrated (only a misleading spec description).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16-17 — `post.user` assumed non-nil; a deleted/anonymized author raises NoMethodError on small_avatar_url.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added embed/best.html.erb the code calls `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` without nil checks, but the diff provides no evidence that `post.user` can be nil in this context. The diff does not change post/user associations, does not show posts being created without a user, and TopicEmbed.import creates posts via PostCreator with a concrete `user`. The proposed scenario (deleted/anonymized author making `post.user` nil) is speculative and not verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — `comments` used with no null check; if #discourse-comments is absent the script throws before registering the listener. Line 7 also assumes discourseUrl has a trailing slash, with no normalization.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the code does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If that element is missing, `comments` is null and this will throw a TypeError, aborting the script before `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` is registered. Also, `iframe.src` is built via `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` with no slash insertion/normalization, so it will produce an invalid path if `discourseUrl` doesn’t already end with `/` (e.g., `https://forum.example.comembed/best`). Both issues are directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:1-7 — depends on globals discourseUrl/discourseEmbedUrl that nothing in the change defines or documents (no generator view, no README, no admin instructions).

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` references `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` without defining them anywhere in the Rails app, but this file is an embed helper intended to be included on an external site (note the `/* global ... */` declarations) where those values are expected to be provided by the embedding page/snippet. Also, none of the new Rails views/layouts include `embed.js`, so the codebase itself doesn’t execute it by default. Therefore the finding is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff; it’s more of a documentation/integration expectation rather than a concrete bug in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4 — neither embed.js nor embed.css.scss is registered for asset precompilation anywhere in the diff, so `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` will raise in production.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new standalone stylesheet `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and uses it via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, but the diff does not add any sprockets manifest require (e.g., into application.css) or any `config.assets.precompile` entry for `embed.css` (or `embed.js`). Under typical Rails/Sprockets production settings (precompile only application.css/js), this results in `embed.css` not being precompiled and the view raising an `AssetNotPrecompiled`-style error at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` also applies to the `loading` render, so the placeholder is cached for a minute after the topic lands.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after the `if/else`. In the `else` branch it does `render 'loading'` but does not `return`, so the response for the loading page will also get the same caching headers. If the topic becomes available shortly after, a client re-requesting the same embed URL may still receive (or reuse) the cached loading response until it expires, making the placeholder persist longer than necessary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:55-76 — docstring says "Convert any relative URLs to absolute" but only root-relative (`/...`) values are rewritten; document-relative (`foo.html`, `../x`) are left broken. Worse, protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x`) also start with `/`, so the leading-slash strip CORRUPTS them into `http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/x`.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, links/images are rewritten only when href/src starts_with?('/') (root-relative). That leaves document-relative URLs like "foo.html" or "../x" unchanged despite the comment claiming to convert relative URLs generally. More importantly, protocol-relative URLs (e.g. "//cdn.example.com/x") also satisfy start_with?('/'), and the code strips all leading slashes via sub(/^\/+/, '') and then prefixes with the embed host, turning it into "<scheme>://<embedhost>/cdn.example.com/x", which is incorrect/corrupts the URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents <<` mutates the caller's String in place; the "imported from" footer is appended to the object PollFeed/import_remote still holds, and double-appends on retry (changing the sha each time).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:147 — topic creation swapped from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` (every imported Disqus topic is now dated at import time) and dropping the `[Permalink](...)` body in favor of scraping the live URL. Turns an offline XML import into one live HTTP fetch per thread with no rescue — a single dead permalink aborts a multi-thousand-thread import mid-way.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Disqus import behavior in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`: it removes the `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), raw: "[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})]", ...)` call and replaces it with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` and Readability parsing with no `rescue`, so a failed HTTP fetch (dead link, timeout, DNS, etc.) will raise and can abort the import run. Also, since `created_at` is no longer passed, imported topics/posts will be timestamped at creation time rather than the Disqus thread's original timestamp. Finally, it changes from using the offline Disqus XML content to scraping the live URL per thread, which is a concrete behavioral regression for an XML-based import.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The single highest-priority item is `best.html.erb:6` — a hard syntax error in the feature's main view, independently confirmed by four lenses and by my own ERB compile, and masked from CI by the nil-returning `TopicView` stub at `embed_controller_spec.rb:50`.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` the header block contains `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby/ERB syntax (Ruby doesn’t support `end if` to close an `if` block). It should be `<%- end %>`. This would cause the template to fail to compile/render at runtime. The controller spec likely doesn’t catch it because Rails controller specs typically don’t render views, and the `TopicView.expects(:new)` expectation returns `nil` by default, so even if views were rendered it would also break when calling `@topic_view.posts`.
